parts.text:
Multiple myeloma is a type of cancer in the bone marrow where some of the stem cells start to produce abnormal blood cells.
• One treatment is to collect stem cells from the bone marrow of the person with multiple myeloma. Healthy stem cells are isolated and grown in the laboratory.
• Radiation is then used to destroy all stem cells and cancerous cells in the bone marrow.
• Finally, large numbers of the healthy stem cells grown in the laboratory are returned to the bone marrow.
Suggest the role of stem cells in this treatment of multiple myeloma.
